message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the most recent common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** and **Perissodactyla**.  
Both lions and zebras belong to the placental‑mammal clade **Laurasiatheria**, so their common ancestor was a small, probably insectivorous or omnivorous mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene. This ancestor would have been a basal member of Laurasiatheria, predating the split that gave rise to the distinct lineages of carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
